market_context: United States/Canada; household dishwasher resets with a clear distinction between canceling a cycle, power-cycling the controls and diagnosing a real fault.
title: How to Reset a Dishwasher

seo.title: How to Reset a Dishwasher Step by Step
seo.meta_description: Learn how to cancel a cycle, power-cycle dishwasher controls safely and recognize when an error needs troubleshooting instead of another reset.
seo.search_intent: Reset a dishwasher that is frozen or unresponsive without erasing useful clues or mistaking a reset for a repair.

excerpt: To reset a dishwasher, try Cancel/Drain first if the controls respond. If the panel remains frozen, remove power for at least one minute, then restore it. Also check Control Lock and make sure the door closes fully. If the same error returns, the reset did not fix the cause and the machine needs troubleshooting.
content_html:
When a dishwasher sits with blinking lights, refuses to start or stops halfway through a program, “resetting” can mean several different things. Sometimes you only need to cancel the active cycle. Sometimes the electronic control needs to lose power briefly. And sometimes the dishwasher is detecting a condition that will return as soon as you start it again.

The most useful sequence is to preserve any error information, cancel the cycle if the panel responds, check the door and Control Lock, then power-cycle the machine only if the controls are still stuck.

Before resetting, save any code or light pattern

If the display shows letters, numbers or a repeating flash pattern, take a photo before you shut the dishwasher down. A reset can temporarily erase that information and make the fault harder to identify when it comes back.

Use the model manual to interpret the code. An error related to filling, draining, temperature or door closure is not repaired by cutting power; a reset can only clear the control state.

If the cycle is still active, try Cancel/Drain

Many dishwashers use Cancel/Drain or an equivalent function to end the current program and run a short drain sequence. Whirlpool advises letting that drain complete before selecting a new cycle on compatible models.

If you can hear spray arms moving, crack the door open slightly first and wait for the spraying action to stop before opening it fully.

Check the door and Control Lock

A dishwasher can appear dead if the door has not latched far enough to close the safety switch. Make sure a pan, rack or utensil is not preventing the door from seating correctly.

Also look for a padlock symbol. Control Lock can prevent the buttons from responding even though the machine has power. The unlock method varies by brand and model.

How to perform a basic power-cycle reset

If the panel remains frozen, a simple power reset is reasonable.

  1. Turn the dishwasher off if the Power button responds.
  2. Unplug it if the plug is accessible. If it is hard-wired, switch off the dedicated circuit breaker.
  3. Wait at least one minute. Whirlpool uses that interval in its dishwasher control-reset guidance.
  4. Restore power.
  5. Close the door firmly, select a cycle and press Start according to your model instructions.

Do not open junction boxes or handle wiring as part of a “reset.” If you cannot confidently identify the correct breaker on a hard-wired unit, stop there.

A reset will not repair a drainage problem

If water remains in the tub and the machine reports a drain error, power-cycling may clear the message briefly but the restriction will still be present.

Check the accessible filter, drain hose and sink or disposer connection as the manual permits. If the dishwasher fails again during the drain stage, the problem is no longer just the interface.

It will not fix a water-supply problem either

If the dishwasher starts but does not fill, confirm the household shutoff valve is open and the supply hose is not kinked. A persistent fill error can involve the valve, sensor or water supply.

Repeated resets cannot open a closed valve or remove a physical blockage.

What if the machine froze after a power outage?

Power interruptions and brief voltage events can leave electronic controls in an odd state. In that situation, a power cycle is especially reasonable. After restoring power, let the panel finish booting before pressing several buttons in quick succession.

If the unit was halfway through a cycle, some models will need Cancel/Drain before they accept a new program.

If the reset works but the fault returns

Watch for the stage where it happens again: fill, wash, heat or drain. That timing helps separate a random control glitch from a repeatable operating problem.

If the same code returns, use the manual and manufacturer support information for that code. At that point the goal is not to reset the dishwasher but to find the condition that is triggering it.

When to call for service

Arrange service if the controls do not recover after a power cycle, the breaker trips, there is an electrical smell, the pump makes abnormal noises, water- or temperature-related errors keep returning or the machine leaks.

Do not continue using a dishwasher that is leaking onto the floor or cabinetry. A small appliance fault can become a much larger moisture problem.

The sequence that preserves useful clues

Photograph the code, use Cancel/Drain if the controls respond, check the door and Control Lock, then remove power for at least one minute if the panel is still frozen. Test once afterward.

If the problem comes back, the dishwasher is telling you it needs diagnosis, not another reset.

faq.question: How long should I leave a dishwasher without power to reset it?
faq.answer: Whirlpool uses at least one minute as a general control power-cycle interval. Your model manual takes priority.

faq.question: Are Cancel and Reset the same thing?
faq.answer: No. Cancel ends the current cycle and often triggers a drain. Resetting the controls means removing and restoring electrical power.

faq.question: Why is the panel not responding if the dishwasher has power?
faq.answer: Control Lock may be active, the door may not be latched correctly or the electronic control may be frozen.

faq.question: Will a reset fix a dishwasher drain error?
faq.answer: Not if there is a blockage or component fault. It may clear the message temporarily, but the cause will return.
